title: Emrys and the Clock
premise: In 1847, Mirabel Amberdale, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Verrin Trading Company on the frozen river town of Coldharbour, is summoned by his dying master to carry a sealed letter naming the company's own directors in a smuggling conspiracy that ruined Mirabel's father. The letter must reach the magistrate in Kingsford before the spring ice breaks and the river reopens — because when it does, the evidence will be destroyed and the family's name buried with it. Pursued through three checkpoints by the company's loyal clerk Halvard Grell, who was once Mirabel's only friend, Mirabel must choose between the loyalty he owes the man who raised him and the truth his father died for. At the third checkpoint, with the ice cracking beneath them, Grell lets him pass at the cost of his own standing; the letter reaches the magistrate, the directors fall, and Mirabel returns not as property but as an heir to nothing but his own name.
about_author: Coral Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing nineteenth-century trading ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes from a drafty house near a slow brown river, where she keeps a broken mantel clock she refuses to have repaired.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On the frozen river at dawn, Mirabel dives beneath the ice for winter pearls, measuring his life in what can be carried: a knife, a ledger stub, his father's diving weight. He establishes the indenture that binds him to Master Verrin. Emotional beat: quiet endurance, the dignity of precision in a hard world.

chapters.title: A House That Keeps Its Own Time
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Inside the Verrin counting-house, the great regulator clock governs every worker's minute, and Mirabel winds it as part of his duties. He glimpses Director Ashcombe arriving unannounced at night, papers changing hands. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in the order Mirabel has trusted.

chapters.title: The Letter Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dying Master Verrin summons Mirabel privately and gives him a sealed letter addressed to the Kingsford magistrate, confessing the company's conspiracy and naming Mirabel's father as an innocent man ruined by it. Verrin dies before explaining everything. Emotional beat: shock curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: What Halvard Taught Me
chapters.summary: Halvard Grell's POV. Flashback woven into present: Grell, the company clerk, remembers teaching young Mirabel his letters and arithmetic, and how he once believed the company was justice made orderly. Now Ashcombe orders him to find 'a missing document.' Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to strain against conscience.

chapters.title: Departure Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel sews the letter into his coat lining and slips out of Coldharbour ahead of the morning bell, taking the ice road south toward Kingsford. He carries almost nothing — deliberately. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of first freedom.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Toll at Marrow Bridge
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At Marrow Bridge, company men search every traveler. Mirabel hides among pearl divers' families he knows, using his father's old reputation to pass. He learns Ashcombe has posted a reward describing him exactly. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into cunning.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sold Warm Bread
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela, a baker's daughter at the bridge town, recognizes Mirabel but says nothing, having lost her own brother to a company debt. She feeds him and warns him the second checkpoint has dogs. Emotional beat: unexpected kindness, the first ally.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Director Ashcombe's POV. Ashcombe calculates the cost of scandal against the cost of murder, coldly deciding the boy must not reach Kingsford. He dispatches Grell personally, trusting his history with Mirabel. Emotional beat: chilling banality of institutional evil.

chapters.title: The White Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Crossing open moorland, Mirabel is caught in a blizzard and nearly dies sheltering in a shepherd's bothy, hallucinating conversations with his drowned father. He questions whether truth is worth dying for. Emotional beat: despair tested and half-answered.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Dogs at Ferren Gate
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At Ferren Gate, the search is thorough and the dogs are trained to paper and ink. Mirabel pays a tanner to mask the letter's scent, then walks through the line with his heart hammering. Emotional beat: nerve-shredding suspense, first true victory.

chapters.title: Grell Catches Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Grell corners Mirabel in a coaching inn outside Ferren — but instead of seizing him, he demands to read the letter. What he reads unmakes twenty years of belief. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted; the hunter learning he was prey too.

chapters.title: Two Men, One Road
chapters.summary: Grell's POV. Grell lets Mirabel go but cannot bring himself to join him, torn between the company that raised him and the truth in the seal. He reports Mirabel 'lost in the blizzard,' buying time. Emotional beat: the agony of divided loyalty.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Speak
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Warm rains come early; the river groans and shifts. Mirabel realizes the ice road home — and the deadline — are both collapsing faster than planned. He abandons the coach route for the river path. Emotional beat: urgency, nature itself becoming antagonist.

chapters.title: What My Father Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In a riverside chapel, Mirabel finds his father's name carved in the divers' memorial wall and finally reads the letter's full contents: not just names, but proof his father died refusing to dive contraband. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Weir at Low Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The final checkpoint guards the last crossing before Kingsford, now flooded with meltwater. The ferryman demands a price Mirabel cannot pay; Ashcombe's riders close behind. Emotional beat: cornered desperation at the story's physical brink.

chapters.title: Grell's Choice
chapters.summary: Grell's POV. Grell arrives at the weir ahead of the riders and holds the ferryman's rope, facing Mirabel across the water. He chooses: he lies to the riders about the route, knowing it ends his career and perhaps his life. Emotional beat: sacrifice as redemption.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The ice dam above the weir bursts. Mirabel crosses in the chaos as the river takes the checkpoint, the ferry, and nearly him — he surfaces clutching his coat, the letter sodden but legible. Emotional beat: cathartic survival, the climax's roar.

chapters.title: Kingsford, Wet Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Half-drowned, Mirabel reaches the magistrate's chambers as clerks try to turn him away. A junior magistrate, moved by the ruined seal and the smudged confession, accepts the testimony and begins depositions. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph, fragile hope.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Ashcombe's POV. As investigators arrive, Ashcombe burns what he can and calculates one final entry — his own flight — but finds every road watched. His arrest is rendered in the same dry accounting language he lived by. Emotional beat: justice as bookkeeping closing its books.

chapters.title: The Price Paid by Others
chapters.summary: Sela's and Grell's POVs. Sela learns her warning mattered; Grel stands trial alongside the directors for his years of silence, refusing to excuse himself. Mirabel testifies on his behalf. Emotional beat: bittersweet accountability — truth costs everyone something.

chapters.title: Free Papers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The magistrate grants Mirabel his freedom papers and restitution from seized company assets — enough to buy back his father's diving weight from the pawnshop and nothing more. He chooses not to stay in Kingsford's new order. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as self-possession.

chapters.title: Winding the Clock
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Returning to Coldharbour, Mirabel winds the great regulator one last time before the counting-house closes, leaving it running for whoever comes next. He walks the river road south with Sela's bread in his pack and his father's weight on his belt. Emotional beat: peace — a life measured now in what he chose to carry.
